observations: Photo 0 shows a clear glass pitcher with measurement markings (100ml to 900ml) and a wooden lid, held by a hand with pink nail polish. A yellow cap covers the spout.
Photo 1 shows the same pitcher on a wooden table, front view, with the wooden lid and yellow spout cap visible. Measurement markings are partially visible.
Photo 2 is a similar front view of the pitcher on the same table, with clearer view of the 300ml and 900ml markings.
The pitcher has a curved handle, a narrow spout, and a wide base. The glass appears thick and durable.
The background in all photos shows shelves with various home goods, suggesting a retail or showroom setting.
No brand name or model is visible on the pitcher in any photo.

claims.claim: It’s made from high-quality, durable clear glass
claims.evidence: Photo 0 and Photo 1 show thick, clear glass with no visible cracks or defects. The glass appears robust and well-made.
Photo 0, Photo 1, and Photo 2 clearly show ml markings (100ml, 300ml, 500ml, 900ml) etched on the glass, which are legible.

risks.risk: Hidden cracks or chips not visible in photos
risks.proof: A close-up shot of the entire pitcher, especially around the base, handle, and spout, under direct light.
risks.if_unproven: priced as potentially damaged, which may reduce value

risks.risk: The wooden lid or yellow spout cap may be loose, warped, or not airtight
risks.proof: A close-up shot of the lid and spout cap being pressed or twisted to show fit and seal.
risks.if_unproven: priced as possibly non-functional or loose, reducing value

risks.risk: The glass may be heat-sensitive or not suitable for hot liquids (if not borosilicate or tempered)
risks.proof: A label or text on the pitcher or packaging indicating material type (e.g., borosilicate, tempered glass).
risks.if_unproven: priced as general-purpose glass, not suitable for hot liquids, which may reduce value

proof_requests: Close-up shot of the pitcher under direct light to check for cracks or chips.
Close-up of the wooden lid and yellow spout cap being pressed or twisted to show fit and seal.
Any label or text on the pitcher or packaging indicating the type of glass (e.g., borosilicate, tempered).
response.reason: The item is clearly a glass pitcher with measurement markings, and the seller's claims about quality and readability are supported by the photos. While there are hidden risks (cracks, lid fit, material type), they are common to such items and do not prevent pricing. The item can be priced at its worst case (e.g., as potentially cracked or not heat-safe) until further proof is provided.
